	<item>
		<title>In Monica Rohan&#8217;s Paintings, Tablecloths and Chairs Uncannily Perch in Remote Landscapes</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/monica-rohan-chair-paintings-invitations/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Thu, 30 Apr 2026 18:54:00 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[landscapes]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Monica Rohan]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[painting]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[textiles]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473505</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan7.jpeg" alt="In Monica Rohan&#8217;s Paintings, Tablecloths and Chairs Uncannily Perch in Remote Landscapes" />Monica Rohan's patterned fabrics and indoor furnishings once again make their way outside, although now, humans are nowhere to be found.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/monica-rohan-chair-paintings-invitations/">In Monica Rohan&#8217;s Paintings, Tablecloths and Chairs Uncannily Perch in Remote Landscapes</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan7.jpeg" alt="In Monica Rohan&#8217;s Paintings, Tablecloths and Chairs Uncannily Perch in Remote Landscapes" />


<p>Home might be a mutable concept, but some objects retain the aura of belonging and comfort even outside the walls we reside in. For <a href="https://www.instagram.com/monrohan/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Monica Rohan</a>, those items are patterned fabrics and bentwood dining chairs, which venture outdoors in her vibrant oil paintings.</p>



<p>The Brisbane-based artist <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/tags/monica-rohan/">has long depicted</a> the supple folds and bright motifs of textiles, which tended to swaddle her characters or hide their faces among natural landscapes. Upholstered loungers and carved wood seats have similarly appeared in unusual spots, precariously holding a figure while nested in a slim hedge or slumping down a small hill. </p>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1401" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan1.jpeg" alt="a painting by Monica Rohan of patterned fabrics floating in a lush landscape with bentwood chairs " class="wp-image-473506" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan1.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan1-640x448.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan1-960x672.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan1-768x538.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan1-1536x1076.jpeg 1536w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Draped Clover&#8221; (2026), oil on board, 70 x 100 centimeters</figcaption></figure>



<p>In recent years, though, Rohan&#8217;s characters have slowly disappeared. Arms that once pulled back a curtain or reached out for stabilization are no longer present, leaving just the domestic objects in place. &#8220;I’ve found this quite freeing, allowing me to explore new ideas about the relationship between people and the landscape,&#8221; the artist tells Colossal, noting that bentwood chairs have become human stand-ins. &#8220;I love their elegant yet rickety construction, and I grew up with them around my kitchen table, so they’re a strong reminder of home for me.&#8221;</p>



<p>Many of the works shown here are part of this transition and will be shown this June at <a href="https://sophiegannongallery.com.au/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Sophie Gannon Gallery</a> in Melbourne for Rohan&#8217;s solo exhibition, <em>Invitations</em>. Against dramatic alpine summits, fast-moving streams, and lush, springtime meadows—scenes derived from the artist&#8217;s hiking trip through Tasmania—plaid tablecloths and crocheted blankets float above the earth as if hung on an imperceptible line strung between two invisible poles. </p>



<p>&#8220;With their exaggerated patterns and strange billowing forms, they appear more ambiguous, wavering between unassuming decoration and smothering intrusion,&#8221; the artist adds. &#8220;From their precarious vantage points, the bentwood chairs no longer offer safe and restful repose. They invite the viewer to join their predicament.&#8221;</p>



<p>Explore more of Rohan&#8217;s paintings on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/monrohan/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img decoding="async" width="2000" height="1553" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan2.jpeg" alt="a painting by Monica Rohan of patterned fabrics floating in a lush stream landscape with bentwood chairs " class="wp-image-473507" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan2.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan2-640x497.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan2-960x745.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan2-768x596.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan2-1536x1193.jpeg 1536w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Flow&#8221; (2026), oil on canvas, 107 x 137 centimeters</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img decoding="async" width="2000" height="2859" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan3.jpeg" alt="a painting by Monica Rohan of a lush floral landscape with a bentwood chair" class="wp-image-473508" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan3.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan3-640x915.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan3-960x1372.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan3-768x1098.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan3-1075x1536.jpeg 1075w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rohan3-1433x2048.jpeg 1433w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Fuzz&#8221; (2026), oil on board, 50 x 35 centimeters</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Dozens of Suspended &#8216;Halos&#8217; Glimmer in a Florentine Factory</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/spy-halos-installation-public-art-bright-festival/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Thu, 30 Apr 2026 17:30:53 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Design]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[immersive]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[installation]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[light]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[SpY]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473547</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-2.jpg" alt="Dozens of Suspended &#8216;Halos&#8217; Glimmer in a Florentine Factory" />SpY's latest installation suspends metallic discs inside of an industrial space as part of Bright Festival.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/spy-halos-installation-public-art-bright-festival/">Dozens of Suspended &#8216;Halos&#8217; Glimmer in a Florentine Factory</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-2.jpg" alt="Dozens of Suspended &#8216;Halos&#8217; Glimmer in a Florentine Factory" />


<p>Earlier this month, dozens of metallic discs suspended from the ceiling of a large industrial space invited viewers to immerse themselves in what <a href="https://spy-urbanart.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">SpY</a> describes as &#8220;a continuous choreography of movement and reflection.&#8221; The artist is known for his <a href="/tags/spy">large-scale installations</a>, often repurposing objects like traffic cones and metallic rescue blankets to create striking urban interventions.</p>



<p>SpY&#8217;s most recent room-scale work, titled &#8220;Halos,&#8221; reimagined the industrial interior of a former railway-related factory in Florence—a place we typically associate with Renaissance elegance as opposed to brutalist design—as part of the city&#8217;s <a href="https://www.brightfestival.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Bright Festival</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-4.jpg" alt="A large interior installation of metallic discs hanging from the ceiling in an industrial space" class="wp-image-473551" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-4-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-4-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-4-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-4-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<p>Three stories high, &#8220;Halos&#8221; interacts with the natural breeze that flows throughout the space, which is exacerbated by people moving around. Glimmering light further lends a sense of ethereality and even magic. </p>



<p>See more on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/spy__studio" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="3000" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-1.jpg" alt="A large interior installation of metallic discs hanging from the ceiling in an industrial space" class="wp-image-473548" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-1-640x960.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-1-960x1440.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-1-768x1152.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-1-1024x1536.jpg 1024w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-1-1365x2048.jpg 1365w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="3000" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-5.jpg" alt="A detail of a large interior installation of metallic discs hanging from the ceiling" class="wp-image-473552" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-5-640x960.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-5-960x1440.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-5-768x1152.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-5-1024x1536.jpg 1024w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-5-1365x2048.jpg 1365w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-3.jpg" alt="A large interior installation of metallic discs hanging from the ceiling in an industrial space" class="wp-image-473550" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-3-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-3-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-3-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/spy-halos-3-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>

]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/sayers-1.jpg" alt="Laura K. Sayers&#8217; Vibrant Postage Stamps Celebrate the Beauty of Everyday Moments" />


<p>From recognizable scenes around her home in Scotland to delicately rendered snapshots of places she visits, <a href="https://www.lauraksayers.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Laura K. Sayers</a>’ meticulously crafted <a href="/tags/laura-k-sayers">postage stamps</a> nod to connections from afar. The artist, who also illustrates children&#8217;s books and is commissioned for special projects like greeting cards, incorporates itty-bitty cuts of colorful paper into tiny tableaux that can fit in the palm of a hand.</p>



<p>Much of the work seen here is currently on view solo in Sayers&#8217; solo exhibition of miniatures titled <em>The Wee Small Hours </em>at <a href="https://www.instagram.com/natelier.41/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">N. atelier</a>. An array of everyday scenes is chronicled in a format we typically associate with significant events and remembrance, documenting fleeting moments like little treasures. Some of her recent pieces are inspired by the Finnish landscape that emerged during the artist&#8217;s stay at the Fiskars Artist-in-Residence program, organized by <a href="https://onoma.fi/en/fiskars-air-en/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Onoma</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1080" height="763" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/sayers-7.jpg" alt="A hand holds a small paper artwork resembling a postage stamp, featuring a Finnish landscape with water and trees" class="wp-image-473544" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/sayers-7.jpg 1080w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/sayers-7-640x452.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/sayers-7-960x678.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/sayers-7-768x543.jpg 768w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1080px) 100vw, 1080px" /></figure>



<p><em>The Wee Small Hours </em>continues through this weekend in Glasgow. And keep an eye out for a joint update from <a href="/tags/tiny-art-show">Tiny Art Show</a>. Find more on Sayers&#8217; <a href="https://www.instagram.com/lauraksayers/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/sayers-4.jpg" alt="A hand holds a small paper artwork resembling a postage stamp, featuring a window with a baker and his goods inside" class="wp-image-473541"/></figure>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Kazumasa-e1777410366193.jpeg" alt="May 2026 Opportunities: Open Calls, Residencies, and Grants for Artists" />


<p>Every month, we share opportunities for artists and designers, including open calls, grants, fellowships, and residencies. Make sure you never miss out by joining our monthly&nbsp;<a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/newsletter/opportunities/">Opportunities Newsletter</a>.</p>



<p><a href="https://www.gallerium.art/scenerium?SCH=76101" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>Scenerium 2026 Art Award: Exhibition, Publication, Sales, and Global Promotion</strong></a><span style="background-color: #ffdc13; padding: 2px 6px; margin-left: 8px; font-size: .9em; font-style: italic;"><strong>Featured</strong></span><br>Where will your art take us? From landscapes and seascapes to cityscapes and imagined worlds, Scenerium 2026 invites artists worldwide to capture the essence of place and turn it into a visual journey. Through natural scenes, urban energy, and visionary environments, this juried opportunity celebrates art that draws viewers in and places them inside the world you create. Selected artists receive a smart online exhibition, Artsy feature, global promotion, catalogue, art magazine publication, press release, visitor engagement, editorial reviews, audience feedback, and exclusive awards. <br>Learn more and submit: <a href="https://www.gallerium.art/scenerium?SCH=76101" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">www.gallerium.art/scenerium</a><br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. PDT on May 7, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><a href="https://hopperprize.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>The Hopper Prize $4,500 Artist Grants</strong></a><span style="background-color: #ffdc13; padding: 2px 6px; margin-left: 8px; font-size: .9em; font-style: italic;"><strong>Featured</strong></span><br>The Hopper Prize is accepting submissions for $4,500 and $1,000 artist grants. Six grants totaling $13,000 USD are available. Two artists will each receive $4,500, and four artists will each receive $1,000. All media is eligible. Additional exposure is available via a 30-artist shortlist, online journal, and Instagram, currently reaching over 165,000.<br><em><strong>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. PDT May 12, 2026.</strong></em></p>



<p>&nbsp;</p>



<p><strong><strong style="font-size: 1.2em;">Open Calls</strong></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.saveartspace.org/wild-free" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">SaveArtSpace Billboard Art Open Call</a></strong> <em>(International)</em><br>SaveArtSpace presents <em>Wild &amp; Free, </em>a public art exhibition on billboard ad space in New York City, opening June 26, 2026, and curated by Gigi Chen. The theme is related to the close connection between nature, mythology, and civilization. There is a $10.99 per image application fee.<br><strong><em>Deadline: May 7, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.yicca.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">YICCA Art Prize</a></strong> <em>(International)</em><br>This competition is open to all media and techniques and geared toward emerging artists, with a total prize pool of €4,500. The application fee varies depending on the number of images submitted and starts at €50.<br><em style=""><b><strong>Deadline: May 7, 2026.</strong></b></em></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://promo.cifra.com/opencall" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">CIFRA Award</a></strong> <em>(International)</em><br>CIFRA welcomes any form of digital art, and the only condition is that it must be possible to submit as a video. Per the theme &#8220;RestArt Reality,&#8221; applicants can share screen-native works that engage with pseudo-evidence, invented archives, alternative chronologies, reconstructions, “false” testimonies, and more. Five winners each receive €1,000.<br><em style=""><b><strong>Deadline: May 8, 2026.</strong></b></em></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.cassart.co.uk/thecassartprize/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Cass Art Prize</a></strong>&nbsp;<em>(U.K. and Ireland)</em><br>The Cass Art Prize 2026, presented by The Cass Group, aims to champion contemporary art from across the U.K. and the Republic of Ireland with a top cash prize of £10,000. Additional awards total more than £20,000, including a Students Award, an Art Educators Award, and more. Winning works will be included in a group exhibition at The Bomb Factory, Marylebone, London, in Autumn 2026.<br><em style=""><b><strong>Deadline: May 8, 2026.</strong></b></em></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://gallery.sunshinecoast.qld.gov.au/art-prizes/sunshine-coast-national-art-prize/entry-form" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Sunshine Coast National Art Prize</a></strong> <em>(Australia)</em><br>The acquisitive Sunshine Coast National Art Prize is a dynamic visual arts award reflecting outstanding contemporary 2D and new media arts practices in Australia. The top prize is AUD $25,000, and the entry fee is AUD $45.<br><strong style="font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Deadline: May 10, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.artistonish.com/p/calls.html" type="link" id="https://www.artistonish.com/p/calls.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Get Published in Artistonish: Visibility, Engagement, and Sales</a></strong> <em>(International)</em><br>The 70th issue of <em>Artistonish Contemporary Art Magazine</em>, published in May 2026, will feature a juried selection of contemporary artworks from around the world, showcased online and on premium glossy pages in print. Each selected work is presented with a full-page image and a dedicated QR code for deeper engagement. Artists will be featured on Artsy, receive a certificate of achievement and exclusive artwork badges, and be promoted through extensive outreach with lasting online visibility in the global art community. Learn more and submit: <a href="https://www.artistonish.com/p/calls.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">www.artistonish.com/calls</a><br><em><strong>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. PDT on May 11, 2026.</strong></em></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://nationalacademy.org/the-academy/grants-and-fellowships/abbey-mural-prize" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Abbey Mural Prize</a></strong> <em>(International)</em><br>The Abbey Mural Prize awards grants to support the creation and restoration of public murals in the United States. Juried by artist and architect members of the National Academy, the Abbey Mural Prize supports projects with grants typically ranging from $10,000 to $40,000. Artists may be from anywhere, but the murals must be in the United States, Tribal Nations, or U.S. territories, including American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands.<br><strong><em>Deadline: May 18, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.artworkarchive.com/call-for-submission/contemporary-craft/2027-elizabeth-r-raphael-founder-s-prize-award-exhibition-contemporary-works-in-small-metals-2026" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">2027 Elizabeth R. Raphael Founder’s Prize Award Exhibition</a></strong> <em>(International)</em><br>The Elizabeth R. Raphael Founder’s Prize was established to recognize excellence in contemporary craft, with a focus on the theme of transformation. The 2027 prize will be awarded for an artwork in small metals. This program offers $5,000, and there is a $45 application fee to submit up to six pieces.<br><strong style="font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Deadline: 11:59 p.m. EDT on May 31, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://opencall.beerslondon.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">BEERS London Group Exhibitions</a></strong> <em>(International)</em><br>This is an opportunity for artists working across all media to apply to be a part of a group exhibition at BEERS London. BEERS&#8217; objective is to discover new, compelling, and contemporary work to present at its gallery. There is a £10 application fee.<br><strong><em>Deadline: June 1, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://artelagunaprize.com/21-edition/" type="link" id="https://artelagunaprize.com/21-edition/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">21st Edition of Arte Laguna Prize</a></strong> <em>(International)</em><br>Apply for this unique opportunity to exhibit your work at the Arsenale Nord in Venice. The finalists’ exhibition will take place from November 6 to 29, 2026. The jury will select 120 finalist artists, including the winner of the first prize of €10,000, among other awards. The application fee is €97.60 (VAT included) for artists under 35 years old and €122 for those 35 and older.<br><strong><em>Deadline: June 30, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p>&nbsp;</p>



<p><strong><strong style="font-size: 1.2em;">Grants</strong></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://franklinfurnace.org/jacki-apple-award/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Franklin Furnace Jacki Apple Award</a></strong><em> (New York City)</em><br>The Jacki Apple Award grants $10,000 to fund a project in performance, media, exhibition, and/or publication by a New York City-based artist working in performance art.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. EDT on May 1, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.tulsaartistfellowship.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Tulsa Artist Fellowship</a></strong> <em>(Tulsa, Oklahoma)</em><br>This unique place-based program will award&nbsp;up to ten artists and arts workers&nbsp;a comprehensive three-year support package in Tulsa, Oklahoma. Each awardee will receive up to&nbsp;$150,000 in financial support,&nbsp;along with a&nbsp;private studio, a&nbsp;$36,000 housing stipend,&nbsp;a&nbsp;$1,500 studio move-in stipend, a&nbsp;$3,600 studio assistant stipend, a&nbsp;$3,600 health and wellness stipend, and&nbsp;access to shared facilities and professional resources&nbsp;designed to sustain ambitious, community-engaged practices over time.<br><strong><em>Deadline: May 7, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://serendipityarts.org/grant/food-matters-grant-2026" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Serendipity Arts Food Matters Grant</a></strong> <em>(India)</em><br>Individual artists or collectives are welcome to apply for this grant of up to 1 Lakh (about $1,050) that emphasizes a knowledge network and supports inquiry into food practices across India. The grant invites researchers, artists, writers, practitioners, and collectives to pursue projects that explore culinary practices at the intersections of literature, politics, technology, and culture.<br><em style="font-weight: bold;"><strong>Deadline: May 8, 2026.</strong></em></p>



<p><a href="https://fundacionbotin.org/en/grants-and-calls-for-applications/plastic-arts-grants/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong><strong>Fundación Botín</strong></strong> <strong>Art Grants</strong></a> <em>(International)</em><br>The Fundación Botín offers six scholarships for artists of any nationality with an expected duration of nine months and a grant of €23,000 each, in addition to medical insurance. One grant is reserved for an artist who is Spanish or a resident in Spain, under 30 years of age, who wants to spend time abroad. Grants cover a period of nine months. Applicants need to register online and also submit physical materials by mail, which must be postmarked by May 8.<br><em style="font-weight: bold;"><strong>Deadline: May 8, 2026.</strong></em></p>



<p><a href="https://www.nyfa.org/awards-grants/rauschenberg-medical-emergency-grants/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>Rauschenberg</strong> <strong>Medical Emergency Grants</strong></a> <em>(U.S.)</em><br>The Rauschenberg Medical Emergency Grants program provides one-time grants of up to $5,000 for recent unexpected medical, dental, and mental health emergencies to artists in financial need who are creating in the visual arts, film/video/electronic/digital arts, and choreography. Applications for the <a href="https://www.nyfa.org/awards-grants/rauschenberg-dancer-emergency-grants/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Rauschenberg Dancer Emergency Grants</a> (up to $3,000) are also open through May 19.<br><em style="font-weight: bold;"><strong>Deadline: 5 p.m. EDT on May 12, 2026.</strong></em></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.nyfa.org/awards-grants/the-jgs-fellowship-for-photography/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">JGS Fellowship for Photography</a></strong> <em>(New York)</em><br>The JGS Fellowship for Photography is an $8,000 cash grant open to New York State photography artists living and working outside of New York City.<br><em style="font-weight: bold;"><strong>Deadline: 5 p.m. EDT on May 19, 2026.</strong></em></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.artprize.org/grants" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">ArtPrize Artist Seed Grant</a></strong> <em>(International</em>)<br>The Artist Seed Grant program supports exceptionally talented emerging artists and designers, helping them bring compelling work to ArtPrize 2026 in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Each selected artist or designer will receive $2,000 to assist with artwork creation and logistical costs, ensuring they can fully participate in the event. These grants help maintain ArtPrize’s accessibility for artists worldwide and at all career stages. In addition to grant opportunities for Grand Rapids-area artists, a venue exhibition grant is also available. Deadlines vary.<br><strong><em>Deadline: May 30, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.gottliebfoundation.org/emergency-grant" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The Adolf and Esther Gottlieb Emergency Grant</a></strong>&nbsp;<em>(International)</em><br>This program provides one-time financial assistance to qualified painters, printmakers, and sculptors whose needs resulted from an unforeseen catastrophic incident and who lack the resources to meet that situation. Awardees typically receive $5,000 and up to $15,000.<br><em><strong>Deadline: Rolling.</strong></em></p>



<p><a href="https://pkf.org/apply/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>Pollock-Krasner Foundation Grant</strong></a><em>&nbsp;(International)</em><br>The foundation welcomes applications from painters, sculptors, and artists working on paper, including printmakers. Grants are intended for one year and range up to $50,000. The artist’s circumstances determine the size of the grant, and professional exhibition history will be considered.<br><em><strong>Deadline: Rolling.</strong></em></p>



<p>&nbsp;</p>



<p><strong style="font-size: 1.2em;">Residencies, Fellowships, &amp; More</strong></p>



<p><a href="https://martinhouse.org/events/residency/#" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>The Martin House Creative Residency</strong> <strong>Program</strong></a>&nbsp;<em>(U.S.)</em><br>This competitive program is open to applicants who seek the resources to support&nbsp;ongoing projects&nbsp;or the&nbsp;creation of new work, with special emphasis on the Frank Lloyd Wright-designed Martin House. Creative makers who are selected to participate will generally spend two to four weeks on site. Residents will receive a stipend of&nbsp;$5,000, and travel expenses of up to $1,000&nbsp;will also be provided to residents from outside New York&#8217;s Buffalo-Niagara region.<br><strong style="font-style: italic;">Deadline: May 13, 2026</strong><strong><em>.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.quinnemanuel.com/artists-in-residence/our-participating-offices/los-angeles-ca" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Quinn Emanuel Los Angeles Residency</a></strong> <em>(Los Angeles)</em><br>This residency is open to emerging and mid-career artists working in all disciplines across Greater Los Angeles. For four months, the artist-in-residence has access to a studio in the Quinn Emanuel Los Angeles office to support their existing practice or a new project. At the end of the residency, an exhibition will be held, and at least one work will be incorporated into the permanent collection. The resident will receive $5,000 per month, for a total of $20,000, plus a materials allowance.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. PDT on May 14, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.dieudonne.org/workspace-2027" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Dieu Donné Workspace Residency Program</a></strong> <em>(New York City metro area)</em><br>With a focus on experimentation and collaboration, Dieu Donné&#8217;s Workspace Residency provides three artists the opportunity to explore paper pulp as an artistic medium. The program includes an introduction to papermaking, six days in the studio with a dedicated collaborator, and a $600 stipend.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. EDT on May 15, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://wsworkshop.org/residencies/studio-residency-grant/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Women&#8217;s Studio Workshop Studio Residency Grant</a></strong> <em>(International)</em><br>The Studio Residency Grant is a six- to eight-week residency for artists to create new work in any of our studio disciplines: intaglio, letterpress, papermaking, screenprinting, or photography. WSW invites applications from artists at any stage in their careers, and the grant includes a stipend of $350 per week, up to $500 for materials used during the residency, up to $250 for travel within the continental U.S., free onsite housing, and 24/7 studio access. Applicants may also opt to be considered for a&nbsp;<a href="https://wsworkshop.org/residencies/studio-workspace-residency/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Studio Workspace Residency</a>&nbsp;or the&nbsp;<a href="https://wsworkshop.org/residencies/anita-wetzel-studio-residency/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Anita Wetzel Residency Grant</a>&nbsp;by checking the corresponding box on their application.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. EDT on May 15, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://monsonarts.org/residencies/overview/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Monson Arts Residency Program</a></strong> <em>(International)</em><br>Monson Arts, in Monson, Maine, supports emerging and established artists and writers by providing them time and space to devote to their creative practices over the course of two or four weeks. A cohort of artists and writers receives private studios, private bedrooms in shared housing, all meals, and a $500 stipend ($250 for two-week programs).<br><strong><em>Deadline: May 15, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.centerforcraft.org/grants-and-fellowships/craft-archive-fellowship" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Center for Craft — Craft Archive Fellowship</a></strong> <em>(International)</em><br>Four fellowships of $5,000 will be awarded to support archival research on underrepresented and non-dominant craft histories in the United States. Funding is intended to support independent research, and proposals are welcome from a range of scholars—both emerging and established—including artist-researchers. Artists may be based anywhere, but must be able to earn taxable income in the U.S.<br><strong><em>Deadline: May 20, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://viaartfund.org/apply/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">VIA Art Fund Artistic Production Grants</a></strong> <em>(International)</em><br>VIA’s Artistic Production Grants fund the production of newly commissioned works of visual art exhibited beyond museum walls, in the public realm, or in non-traditional exhibition environments. &nbsp;These grants are awarded to projects that best exemplify VIA’s three core values of Artistic Production, Thought Leadership, and Public Engagement. Grant amounts range from $25,000 to $100,000.<br><strong><em>Deadline to submit letter of inquiry: May 21, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.fondationgrantham.org/en/residency-artists" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Grantham Foundation Visual Arts Residency</a></strong> <em>(International)</em><br>Grantham Foundation supports established artists whose practices or approaches recognize environmental issues. The four-week residency, which takes place in Saint-Edmond-de-Grantham, Québec, includes a grant of CAD $5,000 to $10,000, depending on the scope of the project.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. EDT on May 27, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.osgf.org/fellowships/eliza-moore-artistic-excellence">Eliza Moore Fellowship for Artistic Excellence</a></strong> <em>(International)</em><br>A program of Oak Spring Garden Foundation, the Eliza Moore Fellowship for Artistic Excellence is awarded annually to one early-career artist who is developing new works that address plants, gardens, or landscapes. This award is open to visual artists, literary artists, dancers, and musicians. The award includes a $10,000 individual grant and requires a two- to five-week stay at Oak Spring in Upperville, Virginia.<br><strong><em>Deadline: May 31, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.headlands.org/program/air/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Headlands Center for the Arts Residencies</a></strong> <em>(International)</em><br>The Artist in Residence program at Headlands Center for the Arts in Sausalito, California, awards fully sponsored residencies to approximately 50 local, national, and international artists each year. Residencies of four to ten weeks include studio space, chef-prepared meals, housing, travel, and living expenses.<br><strong><em>Deadline: June 1, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://residenciacorazon.com.ar/artist-residency-program-argentina-residencia-corazon/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Residencia Corazón</a></strong><em> (International)</em><br>Residencia Corazón is an independent, artist-run residency in La<br>Plata, Argentina—a home for artists since 2006. The program welcomes visual<br>artists, writers, curators, and creative researchers from around the<br>world for one- to three-month residencies. Each stay is fully personalized, and fees range from $800 to $1,500 per month.<br><strong><em>Deadline: Rolling.</em></strong></p>

		<item>
		<title>Linocuts by Eduardo Robledo Celebrate Mexican Heritage and Community</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/eduardo-robledo-linocuts-mexico-city/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Wed, 29 Apr 2026 17:02:12 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Illustration]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Eduardo Robledo]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[linocuts]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Mexico]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[printmaking]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473483</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-6.jpg" alt="Linocuts by Eduardo Robledo Celebrate Mexican Heritage and Community" />Robledo draws on his upbringing in the Mexico City borough of Xochimilco for bold prints.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/eduardo-robledo-linocuts-mexico-city/">Linocuts by Eduardo Robledo Celebrate Mexican Heritage and Community</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-6.jpg" alt="Linocuts by Eduardo Robledo Celebrate Mexican Heritage and Community" />


<p>In the richly detailed linocuts of <a href="https://www.eduardorobledo.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Eduardo Robledo</a>, festive ceremonies, spiritual motifs, and dream-like interactions unfurl. The Mexico City-based artist was born and raised in the southern borough of Xochimilco, which is famous for its canals—vestiges of a huge Aztec water transport system still used today for bringing goods into the city. This area and its time-honored customs provide a bounty of inspiration for Robledo.</p>



<p>Community and celebration are at the heart of his work, as creatures and figures converge in enigmatic, sometimes ritualistic choreographies. Traditional motifs like skulls and skeletons, which represent remembrance, joy, and an acceptance of the cycle of life and death, interact with denizens of the region like armadillos, birds, reptiles, and more.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1920" height="1297" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-3.jpg" alt="a linocut print by Eduardo Robleno of a peacock and an armadillo on either side of an upside-down rose" class="wp-image-473486" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-3.jpg 1920w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-3-640x432.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-3-960x649.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-3-768x519.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-3-1536x1038.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1920px) 100vw, 1920px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Adiós&#8221; (2021), three-color linocut, 15 x 22 inches</figcaption></figure>



<p>Social activism has also played a strong role in Robledo&#8217;s practice, tapping into the power of printmaking to spread messages about causes he cares deeply about. &#8220;Printmaking is democratic; it’s more supportive,&#8221; he shares in <a href="https://hechoamano.org/post/2255-eduardo-robledo-art-with-a-sense-of-community" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">a profile</a>. &#8220;There is a very strong graphic arts tradition in social movements.&#8221;</p>



<p>Robledo&#8217;s compositions are playful yet mysterious, universal and also arcane. Winged hearts, known as <em>Sagrado Corazón, </em>or the Sacred Heart, symbolize love, healing, and spiritual devotion. Armadillos represent protection and abundance, and numerous other foods, plants, and nods to culture—such as Xochimilco&#8217;s colorful canal boats known as <em>trajineras</em>—are venerated in scenes of dancing or totem-like configurations.</p>



<p>Robled&#8217;s prints can be found at <a href="https://hechoamano.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Hecho a Mano</a> in Santa Fe, and the artist is also a co-founder of <a href="https://lugardehuida.com/en/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Lugar de Huida</a> in Mexico City, a gallery highlighting Mexican printmakers. See more on the artist&#8217;s <a href="https://www.instagram.com/eduardorobledomx/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-2.jpg" alt="a linocut print by Eduardo Robleno of an armadillo or reptile-like creature with a huge cornucopia of flowers and other motifs on its back" class="wp-image-473485"/><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Arbol de la Vida&#8221; (2025), linocut, 30 x 22 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1920" height="1323" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-7.jpg" alt="a linocut print by Eduardo Robleno of dancing skeletons, birds, and other creatures" class="wp-image-473490" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-7.jpg 1920w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-7-640x441.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-7-960x662.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-7-768x529.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-7-1536x1058.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1920px) 100vw, 1920px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Carnaval&#8221; (2023), linocut, 15 x 22 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1920" height="2605" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-1.jpg" alt="a linocut print by Eduardo Robleno of two skeletons inside of a larger motif of a skull-headed figure, holding a hybrid bird-tree" class="wp-image-473484" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-1.jpg 1920w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-1-640x868.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-1-960x1303.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-1-768x1042.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-1-1132x1536.jpg 1132w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-1-1509x2048.jpg 1509w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1920px) 100vw, 1920px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;El Pacto&#8221; (2024), linocut, 15 x 11 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1920" height="2772" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-9.jpg" alt="a linocut print by Eduardo Robleno of an armadillo amid a number of red hearts with winds" class="wp-image-473492" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-9.jpg 1920w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-9-640x924.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-9-960x1386.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-9-768x1109.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-9-1064x1536.jpg 1064w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-9-1419x2048.jpg 1419w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1920px) 100vw, 1920px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Soltar&#8221; (2024), three-color linocut, 22 x 15 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1920" height="2453" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-10.jpg" alt="a linocut print by Eduardo Robleno of a figure perched atop a group of compartments with snakes and other motifs" class="wp-image-473493" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-10.jpg 1920w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-10-640x818.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-10-960x1227.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-10-768x981.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-10-1202x1536.jpg 1202w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-10-1603x2048.jpg 1603w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1920px) 100vw, 1920px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Hombres de Conocimiento&#8221; (2020), linocut, 44 x 30 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1920" height="2613" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-5.jpg" alt="a linocut print by Eduardo Robleno of a deer standing over purple agave plants, in front of an orange sun, looking at an anatomical heart" class="wp-image-473488" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-5.jpg 1920w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-5-640x871.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-5-960x1307.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-5-768x1045.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-5-1129x1536.jpg 1129w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/robleno-5-1505x2048.jpg 1505w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1920px) 100vw, 1920px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;El Camino&#8221; (2026), serigraph, 15 x 11 inches</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Spell Your Name with NASA&#8217;s Earthly Alphabet of Aerial Images</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/nasa-usgs-your-name-in-landsat-earth-day/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Wed, 29 Apr 2026 12:44:26 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Design]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Photography]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Science]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[aerial]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Earth]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[interactive]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[landscapes]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[NASA]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[rivers]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473494</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/landsat-2.jpeg" alt="Spell Your Name with NASA&#8217;s Earthly Alphabet of Aerial Images" />Landsat, a NASA and USGS program, has documented the surface of Earth from space since 1972.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/nasa-usgs-your-name-in-landsat-earth-day/">Spell Your Name with NASA&#8217;s Earthly Alphabet of Aerial Images</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/landsat-2.jpeg" alt="Spell Your Name with NASA&#8217;s Earthly Alphabet of Aerial Images" />


<p>From rivers and oxbow lakes to crop-field patchworks and mineral sediments, <a href="https://science.nasa.gov/mission/landsat/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Landsat</a> has seen it all. A program of <a href="/tags/nasa" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">NASA</a> and <a href="https://www.usgs.gov/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">USGS</a>, the satellite initiative has documented the Earth&#8217;s surface since 1972, making it the longest continuous record of our planet&#8217;s ever-evolving landscapes. And to mark Earth Day 2026, the organizations launched a playful way to interact with some of their findings collected over the past five-and-a-half decades—<a href="https://science.nasa.gov/specials/your-name-in-landsat/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">a name generator</a>.</p>



<p>Using the tool is simple: type in your name, or any word, and Landsat returns it in the form of vertical snapshots of a wide range of terrain. Just like we see with <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2025/08/nasa-mars-blue-skies/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">composites of Mars</a>, for instance, scientists have digitally enhanced some images to highlight specific features. Those used for &#8220;Your Name in Landsat&#8221; sport a wide array of hues, textures, and patterns that glimpse the diversity of our planet&#8217;s surface.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2554" height="717" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/landsat-11.jpeg" alt="Eight vertical frames of the earth's surface captured from NASA's Landsat program with landforms that loosely resemble letters of the alphabet, arranged to spell &quot;COLOSSAL&quot;" class="wp-image-473497" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/landsat-11.jpeg 2554w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/landsat-11-640x180.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/landsat-11-960x270.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/landsat-11-768x216.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/landsat-11-1536x431.jpeg 1536w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/landsat-11-2048x575.jpeg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2554px) 100vw, 2554px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Colossal&#8221;</figcaption></figure>



<p>Landsat is an incredible resource that features time-lapses of changing land use over several decades. Even this playful name generator allows you to hover over individual images and learn the exact locations—down to the coordinates—and all of the program&#8217;s data is <a href="https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/landsat-data-access" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">publicly accessible</a>. For example, the &#8220;C&#8221; in &#8220;Colossal&#8221; above is a vertical view of a cloud-speckled Deception Island in Antarctica, and the &#8220;A&#8221; is the uniquely shaped Lake Mjøsa in Norway.</p>



<p>You might also enjoy <em><a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2020/08/overview-timelapse-book/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Overview</a></em>, a book that chronicles how the landscape has changed over time. Learn more about Landsat from <a href="https://science.nasa.gov/mission/landsat/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">NASA</a>. (via <a href="https://petapixel.com/2026/04/27/you-can-spell-your-name-is-aerial-images-thanks-to-nasa/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">PetaPixel</a>)</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/nasa-usgs-your-name-in-landsat-earth-day/">Spell Your Name with NASA&#8217;s Earthly Alphabet of Aerial Images</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></content:encoded>
					
		
		
			</item>
		<item>
		<title>Lina Lapelytė Fills Hamburger Bahnhof with 400,000 Wood Blocks for Communal Building</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/lina-lapelyte-we-make-years-out-of-hours/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Tue, 28 Apr 2026 21:35:23 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[community art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[installation]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Lina Lapelytė]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[wood]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473459</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/lina-1.jpg" alt="Lina Lapelytė Fills Hamburger Bahnhof with 400,000 Wood Blocks for Communal Building" />"We Make Years Out of Hours" invites the public to remake structures from 10-centimeter blocks.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/lina-lapelyte-we-make-years-out-of-hours/">Lina Lapelytė Fills Hamburger Bahnhof with 400,000 Wood Blocks for Communal Building</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/lina-1.jpg" alt="Lina Lapelytė Fills Hamburger Bahnhof with 400,000 Wood Blocks for Communal Building" />


<p>Inside the cavernous former train station that now houses <a href="https://www.smb.museum/en/home/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Hamburger Bahnhof</a>, 400,000 wooden cubes stack and topple into piles. Conceived by Lithuanian artist <a href="https://www.linalapelyte.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Lina Lapelytė</a> and commissioned by Chanel, &#8220;We Make Years Out of Hours&#8221; is a large-scale installation that invites the public to remake structures from these 10-centimeter blocks made of pine and spruce.</p>



<p>Lapelytė often combines sound and performance and collaborates with both professionals and novices. This participatory work continues the artist&#8217;s interest in collective making and caretaking, particularly as it relates to shared authorship and how we might amend and reshape what currently exists.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/lina-8.jpg" alt="people work on an installation of wooden blocks by Lina Lapelytė in a cavernous building" class="wp-image-473462" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/lina-8.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/lina-8-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/lina-8-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/lina-8-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/lina-8-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<p>A trio of weekly performances on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays will feature a libretto with the words of 15 writers, including Vietnamese-American poet Ocean Vuong, Lebanese-American painter Etel Adnan, Iranian filmmaker <br>Forugh Farrokhzad, and Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish. Centered around community, love, and loss, these songs create another dimension in the space to consider agency and hope.</p>



<p>&#8220;We Make Years Out of Hours&#8221; opens on May 1 and is on view through January 10, 2027, in Berlin. Explore more of Lapelytė&#8217;s multi-disciplinary works on <a href="https://www.linalapelyte.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">her website</a> and <a href="https://www.instagram.com/linalapelyte/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="3000" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/lina-7.jpg" alt="a man works on an installation of wooden blocks by Lina Lapelytė in a cavernous building" class="wp-image-473461" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/lina-7.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/lina-7-640x960.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/lina-7-960x1440.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/lina-7-768x1152.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/lina-7-1024x1536.jpg 1024w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/lina-7-1365x2048.jpg 1365w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>

		<title>7 Artists Discuss the Power and Urgency of Textiles</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/7-artists-on-soft-sculptures-film/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Tue, 28 Apr 2026 16:43:55 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Film]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[fiber art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[installation]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[sculpture]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[short film]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[textiles]]></category>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/soft-2.jpg" alt="7 Artists Discuss the Power and Urgency of Textiles" />"We live with so many hard things," says Sheila Hicks, "that we're crying for softness." </p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/7-artists-on-soft-sculptures-film/">7 Artists Discuss the Power and Urgency of Textiles</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/soft-2.jpg" alt="7 Artists Discuss the Power and Urgency of Textiles" />


<p>&#8220;We live with so many hard things,&#8221; says Sheila Hicks, &#8220;that we&#8217;re crying for softness.&#8221; The pleasure, simplicity, and tactile qualities of textiles ground a new film from Louisiana Channel, which explores the ways in which fiber art remains both evocative and relevant in this increasingly digital era.</p>



<p>&#8220;<a href="https://vimeo.com/1185838727" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">7 Artists on Soft Sculptures</a>&#8221; weaves together a variety of distinct approaches to textiles. Nick Cave describes incorporating found plastics, toys, metals, fringe, and more into <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/tags/nick-cave/">elaborate suits</a> that mask the wearer&#8217;s identity, while Icelandic artist Shoplifter shares her obsessions with brightly dyed synthetic hair, which she transforms into immersive installations.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-embed is-type-video is-provider-vimeo wp-block-embed-vimeo wp-embed-aspect-16-9 wp-has-aspect-ratio"><div class="wp-block-embed__wrapper">
<iframe loading="lazy" title="7 Artists On Soft Sculptures" src="https://player.vimeo.com/video/1185838727?dnt=1&amp;app_id=122963" width="500" height="281" frameborder="0" allow="autoplay; fullscreen; picture-in-picture; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"></iframe>
</div></figure>



<p>And Kaarina Kaikkonen offers her deeply personal reason for incorporating used clothing into her large-scale installations: &#8220;When I was 14, after my father&#8217;s death, I wanted to wear his clothes,&#8221; she says. &#8220;I felt very strongly that my father is near me if I wear his clothes.&#8221; This invisible presence continues to inform her work, offering a connection to people and times passed.</p>



<p>Louisiana Channel hosts a trove of videos featuring artists, writers, and designers, including earlier studio visits with <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2022/04/chiharu-shiota-string-installations/">Shiota</a> and <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2021/09/shoplifter-hair-installations/">Shoplifter</a>, on <a href="https://vimeo.com/louisianachannel" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Vimeo</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2500" height="1522" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/soft-1.jpg" alt="ernesto neto sits on the floor while touching his sculpture" class="wp-image-473451" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/soft-1.jpg 2500w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/soft-1-640x390.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/soft-1-960x584.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/soft-1-768x468.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/soft-1-1536x935.jpg 1536w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/soft-1-2048x1247.jpg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2500px) 100vw, 2500px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Ernesto Neto</figcaption></figure>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? 		<item>
		<title>From Micro to Mega, Jon McCormack&#8217;s Striking Photos Reveal Nature&#8217;s Patterns</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/jon-mccormack-patterns-art-nature-photography-book/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Tue, 28 Apr 2026 12:59:53 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Books]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Nature]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Photography]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[aerial]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[animals]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Jon McCormack]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[landscapes]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[micro]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[pattern]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[wildlife]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473423</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-5.jpg" alt="From Micro to Mega, Jon McCormack&#8217;s Striking Photos Reveal Nature&#8217;s Patterns" />The idea for 'Patterns: Art of the Natural World' emerged from a period of quiet reflection.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/jon-mccormack-patterns-art-nature-photography-book/">From Micro to Mega, Jon McCormack&#8217;s Striking Photos Reveal Nature&#8217;s Patterns</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-5.jpg" alt="From Micro to Mega, Jon McCormack&#8217;s Striking Photos Reveal Nature&#8217;s Patterns" />


<p>Growing up in the Australian Outback, where he first picked up a camera as a teenager to document his surroundings in the bush, <a href="https://jonmccormack.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Jon McCormack</a> developed a keen eye for the beauty and subtleties of nature. Throughout his career, he&#8217;s stepped foot on all seven continents. Yet the idea for his new book, <em>Patterns: Art of the Natural World</em>, emerged from a period of quieter reflection.</p>



<p>Like many of us during the pandemic, McCormack&#8217;s travels were limited to his immediate area. He began visiting the same spots repeatedly and &#8220;discovered a new way of seeing, using photography to reveal the hidden harmony and symmetry of the natural world,&#8221; says a statement. <em>Patterns, </em>forthcoming from Damiani Books, draws upon this patient and attentive approach to nature&#8217;s rhythms, emphasizing its interconnectedness, resilience, and fragility.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1500" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-6.jpg" alt="a photograph by Jon McCormack of bright yellow aspen trees along the edge of a lake in the mountains" class="wp-image-473429" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-6-640x480.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-6-960x720.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-6-768x576.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-6-1536x1152.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Golden aspens and their reflection join to shape a luminous triangle of color</figcaption></figure>



<p>The snapshots view slivers of our world from a range of perspectives, whether honing in on the recurring features of crystals or flying over a flamboyance of flamingos in Kenya. <em>Patterns </em>contains 90 striking images and text contributions from fellow photographers and conservationists.</p>



<p>Find your copy on <a href="https://bookshop.org/a/96/9788862088572" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Bookshop</a>, and keep up with McCormack&#8217;s travels on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/jonmccormackphoto/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1500" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-3.jpg" alt="a photograph by Jon McCormack of an aerial view of streams that look abstract" class="wp-image-473426" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-3-640x480.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-3-960x720.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-3-768x576.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-3-1536x1152.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Patterns of minerals left behind by volcanic eruptions in Iceland</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2667" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-4.jpg" alt="a photograph by Jon McCormack of an abstract pattern in nature" class="wp-image-473427" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-4-640x853.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-4-960x1280.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-4-768x1024.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-4-1152x1536.jpg 1152w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-4-1536x2048.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">A microscope reveals the crystalline patterns of caffeine</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-8.jpg" alt="a photograph by Jon McCormack of prismatic spray above a waterfall in Yosemite National Park" class="wp-image-473431" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-8.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-8-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-8-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-8-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-8-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">A prismatic waterfall at Yosemite</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-2.jpg" alt="a photograph by Jon McCormack of birds flying over yellow streams, seen from high in the air" class="wp-image-473425" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-2.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-2-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-2-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-2-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-2-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Flamingos in flight mirror the shifting patterns etched across Kenya’s Lake Magadi</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2667" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-1.jpg" alt="a photograph by Jon McCormack of dolphins swimming, seen from a vertical perspective" class="wp-image-473424" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-1-640x853.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-1-960x1280.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-1-768x1024.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-1-1152x1536.jpg 1152w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/mccormack-1-1536x2048.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">A pod of dolphins swim near the Channel Islands</figcaption></figure>

		<title>Cassandra Dias Takes an Impressionistic Approach to Painting with Thread</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/cassandra-dias-richly-stitched-landscape-embroidery-book/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Mon, 27 Apr 2026 18:19:00 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Books]]></category>

		<category><![CDATA[Cassandra Dias]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[embroidery]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[fiber art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[landscapes]]></category>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dias-9.jpg" alt="Cassandra Dias Takes an Impressionistic Approach to Painting with Thread" />What better way to meditate on nature's most majestic features than to recreate its details one stitch at a time?</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/cassandra-dias-richly-stitched-landscape-embroidery-book/">Cassandra Dias Takes an Impressionistic Approach to Painting with Thread</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dias-9.jpg" alt="Cassandra Dias Takes an Impressionistic Approach to Painting with Thread" />


<p>What better way to meditate on nature&#8217;s most majestic features than to recreate its details one stitch at a time? Since picking up a needle and thread in 2020, <a href="https://www.cassandramdias.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Cassandra Dias</a> has translated rugged cliffsides, neat vineyards, and sun-streaked mountains into <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2022/09/cassandra-dias-embroideries/">lush embroideries</a>. </p>



<p>The Southern California-based artist uses a technique known as thread painting, which combines a variety of stitches to create richly textured scenes. Having developed a dreamy, impressionistic style, Dias&#8217; embroideries mimic the pointed and gestural movements of a paintbrush, with the depth of impasto. Whether depicting a single autumnal tree or a wide seascape stretching for miles, the artist&#8217;s works direct attention to the minuscule details and the abundant life all around us.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1998" height="2505" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dias-8.jpg" alt="a process shot of hands creating a lush landscape embroidery in a light wood hoop by Cassandra Dias" class="wp-image-473415" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dias-8.jpg 1998w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dias-8-640x802.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dias-8-960x1204.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dias-8-768x963.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dias-8-1225x1536.jpg 1225w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dias-8-1633x2048.jpg 1633w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1998px) 100vw, 1998px" /></figure>



<p>Many of the images shown here are from Dias&#8217; forthcoming book, <em>Richly Stitched Landscape Embroidery: Mastering Thread Painted Scenes</em>, which will be released in May. To dive into her techniques and distinctive approach, pre-order your copy from the <a href="https://colossal.shop/products/richly-stitched-landscape-embroidery-pre-order" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Colossal Shop</a>. You can also find more on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/cassiemdias/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1655" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dias-1.jpg" alt="a collection of lush landscape embroideries in light wood hoops by Cassandra Dias" class="wp-image-473408" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dias-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dias-1-640x530.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dias-1-960x794.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dias-1-768x636.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/dias-1-1536x1271.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>
